issue.title: Route for parent component not matched if no child is mapped to primary outlet
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")

```
[x] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior** 

<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->

When a component contains child components it is only found by the router if one of the child components is mapped to the primary outlet. If e.g. a component contains two router outlets named "primary2" and "secondary" it results in the router failing to find the containing component (route to container called here: "nokcontainer") and throws an exception: core.umd.js:3427 EXCEPTION: Uncaught (in promise): Error: Cannot match any routes: 'nokcontainer'.

I traced the issue down to the place where the remainder of the path is matched against the child routes but did not get further. The matching for the "nokcontainer" triggers but then the code starting here attempting to match the children throws somewhere deep down the exception.

```
                var rawSlicedSegments_1 = segments.slice(lastChild);
                var childConfig$ = this.getChildConfig(injector, route);
                return rxjs_operator_mergeMap.mergeMap.call(childConfig$, function (routerConfig) {
```

**Expected behavior**

As a naive user I assume router-outlets are behaving the same whether they are primary outlets or not. I also assume as a naive user that adding children to a route should not cause the parent route not to be found anymore as such an exception is misleading.

I could not find any documentation that there must be always a primary child outlet. On the other hand I saw several examples on Stackoverflow with not accepted answers where a list of named child routes were given as suggestion that did not not include the "primary" route.

I also suspect the issue here may be the causing the issue here: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/11208

**Reproduction of the problem**

http://plnkr.co/edit/f2pD1oQx9A6o7Tq3gAfm?p=preview

Home component: obvious
OK  container: child1 child2 in outlets named primary and secondary
NOK container: child 1 child2 in outlets named primary**2** and secondary -> exception

issue.title: Secondary routes/segments don't map to browser buttons when lazy loading a module that defines routes
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")

```
[x] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior**
Scenario: You have a lazy loaded module that defines its own secondary route/segment.
When the secondary route is triggered, pressing the Back button on the browser reflects a URL change, but the content from the secondary route stays on the page. Pressing Forward afterwards does not replace the current content, but instead adds a copy of the content to the page.

**Expected behavior**
Pressing the Back button should remove the content that was loaded from the lazy loaded module.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
1. See the plnkr: [http://plnkr.co/edit/mYrqjW?p=preview](http://plnkr.co/edit/mYrqjW?p=preview)
2. Click the blue button on the top-right of the preview section to launch the preview in a separate window (this will allow you to go forward and back in the browser). 
3. Click the "About (lazy)" link to lazy load the About module. The About heading should display on the page and the url should be "/home(lazy:about)"
4. Press backspace or Alt-Left (depending on your browser) to go to the previous page. The url should be "/home". The content from the About module remains on the page.
- **Angular version:** 2.0.2
  
  <!-- Check whether this is still an issue in the most recent Angular version -->
- **Language:** [all]
- **Node (for AoT issues):** `node --version` = 4.5.0
